title: Chennai Love Story Crosses ₹25 Crore Worldwide in Opening Weekend
excerpt: Kiran Abbavaram's Telugu romantic drama earns ₹17 crore net domestically in three days, surpassing his previous hit SK Kalyana Mandapam to become his third-highest-grossing film.
body:
• Chennai Love Story collected ₹6.25 crore net on Day 3, bringing its three-day India net total to ₹17 crore and worldwide gross past ₹25 crore.
  • The film has already surpassed SK Kalyana Mandapam (₹11.31 crore) to become Kiran Abbavaram's third-highest-grossing film, with his career record of ₹26.94 crore now within reach.
  • Made on a budget of ₹30 crore, the film has recovered over 50% of its production costs and needs roughly ₹13 crore more to reach the safe zone.
  • Strong word of mouth and a clear two-week window without major Telugu competition could propel the film toward breakeven and beyond.

Kiran Abbavaram's Chennai Love Story continued its upward trajectory at the box office on Day 3, collecting an estimated ₹6.25 crore net in India on Sunday—its highest single-day haul since release. The Telugu romantic drama, which opened on July 24, has now amassed approximately ₹17 crore net domestically and crossed the ₹25 crore mark in worldwide gross collections.

Day-Wise Breakdown and Weekend Momentum

The film opened to ₹4.95 crore net on its first day and climbed to ₹5.5 crore on Saturday before posting its best day yet on Sunday. The consistent upward trend over the opening weekend is a strong signal for a mid-budget Telugu film that released without the backing of a major star franchise.

https://x.com/Koimoi/status/2083143131839832447

Day-wise India net collections stand at: Day 1 — ₹4.95 crore, Day 2 — ₹5.5 crore, Day 3 — ₹6.25 crore, for a running total of approximately ₹17 crore. Overseas markets contributed nearly ₹5 crore gross, with North America alone accounting for around $400,000.

A Career Milestone for Kiran Abbavaram

With its three-day haul, Chennai Love Story has surpassed SK Kalyana Mandapam, which earned ₹11.31 crore during its entire theatrical run, to become the third-highest-grossing film of Kiran Abbavaram's career. The actor's current record is held by KA (2024), which collected ₹26.94 crore net—a figure that now looks achievable if the film sustains its weekday hold.

"The film witnessed excellent growth on Sunday, recording its highest single-day collections in the Telugu states."

— TeluguCinema.com

Budget Recovery and Path to Profitability

Produced on a reported budget of ₹30 crore by Srinivasa Kumar and Sai Rajesh under Mass Movie Makers and Amrutha Productions, Chennai Love Story has recovered over 50% of its production costs through domestic collections alone. The film's pre-release business was pegged at ₹15 crore worldwide, and trade estimates suggest it needs approximately ₹16 crore in distributor share to break even. With an estimated ₹13 crore share already earned, the gap stands at roughly ₹3 crore—a target that looks realistic given current momentum.

Audience Reception and Competition

Directed by Ravi Namburi with music by Mani Sharma, the film stars Abbavaram as Steven Shankar, an orphan who moves to Chennai to pursue a career in the film industry, and Sri Gouri Priya as Nivedita. The film's interval twist has emerged as a major talking point, driving strong word of mouth particularly among younger audiences. Critics have offered mixed assessments—praising the lead performances and first half while noting that the second half loses some momentum.

Crucially, the film benefits from a favorable release window. Several Telugu filmmakers delayed their projects to avoid clashing with the much-anticipated Jana Nayagan, and with no major Telugu releases expected over the next two weeks, Chennai Love Story has a clear runway to extend its theatrical run.

What's Next

The coming weekdays will be the real test. If the film can hold above ₹2-3 crore daily through the first week, it should comfortably cross the ₹25 crore net mark domestically and move into striking distance of Abbavaram's career-best. By Day 5, early reports suggest the film had already crossed ₹23 crore net in India, placing it among Tollywood's top 10 highest-grossing films of 2026. For a content-driven mid-budget film without a massive pre-release franchise pull, those are numbers that reaffirm the commercial viability of well-executed romantic dramas in Telugu cinema.
